A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LensGNN research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original node and molecular graph classification results, component ablations, backbone comparisons, and efficiency and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds ensemble comparisons, one-shot evaluations, another backbone test, and further sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage alignment and LoRA ensembling procedure is retained. Although Section 4.1 replaces 'shared linear layer' with 'shared MLP' and describes freezing it, v2 Figure 2 already depicts both the MLP and its freezing. The added neighbor-sampling description does not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five node classification datasets—Cora, PubMed, ogbn-arXiv, Citeseer and Wiki-CS—and three molecular classification datasets—BACE, BBBP and ClinTox. The added experiments vary label budgets, model configurations and input limits within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds SciBERT and MedBERT to Table 1, Bagging, Stacking and AdaBoost comparisons for GNN ensembles in Table 4, and Bagging/Stacking comparisons combining LLM and GNN predictions in Table 13. These substantially expand the comparator set, particularly for the central ensembling proposal. InstructGLM was already evaluated in v2.

E3.justification: v3 adds one-shot evaluations, a LLaMA2-7B backbone test, ensemble-size experiments extending to five GNNs with InternLM2.5-7B and t=4, and input-budget experiments spanning 0.5K–1.75K tokens. These substantially expand the evaluation design. Existing dataset splits and the retained hyperparameter tables are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices I–K add substantial analyses of whether additional GNNs continue helping and how input length affects accuracy and training cost. Graph-token sensitivity is also extended from Cora/PubMed to Citeseer/Wiki-CS. The original component ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional tables and plots continue to report point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing matched benchmark and ablation values are retained, while v3 adds extensive comparator, one-shot, backbone, ensemble-size and input-length results, including 94.59% for LLaMA2-7B on PubMed. Some new entries conflict with retained tables: Table 14 reports PubMed LLaGA accuracy as 75.01%, whereas Table 2 in both versions gives 94.45%; 75.01% is its ogbn-arXiv entry. Table 4 also assigns some best-variant scores to LensGNN-ALL.

T1.justification: The graph definitions and Equations 1–4 are retained. The added o = LLM(...) expression summarizes the previously described prompt-to-label mapping rather than introducing substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: LLMs can ensemble multiple GNNs through two-stage alignment, yielding strong classification performance, whereas small language models struggle with ensembling. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations attributing three-GNN versus two-GNN underperformance to limited data and noise, discusses saturation when adding GNNs, and recommends selecting three or four models using validation performance. It also discusses scarce-label failures and the information-versus-cost tradeoff of longer inputs. The formal limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the 20-neighbor cap and random sampling, identifies the best variants behind existing starred results, and supplies additional baseline-backbone information and input-dependent training times. Existing implementation settings, hardware, hyperparameter tables and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations and descriptions for classical ensemble methods, SciBERT, MedBERT and TAPE, and expands baseline characterization in Appendix B. The main related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain intact. TAPE is discussed through another work's reported comparison, without becoming an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify alignment and prompt construction, and terminology and the author list are edited. Prompt-design principles move from Section 4.2 to Appendix D, while the original hyperparameter Appendix E becomes Appendix L. Most existing main-text prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 2 with explicit connections between training stages, expands Table 1, and adds seven tables and two analysis figures. Table captions, sizing and placements are extensively revised. Figures 1 and 3–6 retain their original visual content despite resizing or relocation.

improvement.justification: The conventional-ensemble controls address a meaningful gap in v2, while the added scaling and input-length analyses provide useful practical guidance. Variant identification and sampling details improve transparency. However, Table 4 labels Cora/Wiki-CS best two-GNN scores as LensGNN-ALL, and Table 14 places some ogbn-arXiv baseline values in its PubMed column. These reporting inconsistencies temper the benefits and limit confidence in parts of the added evidence.
